In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman's Wife. Now let's take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. ( ⓐ ) After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother's encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. ( ⓑ ) Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. ( ⓒ ) Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. ( ⓓ ) She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. ( ⓔ ) In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day. Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in appreciating these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.
solution: 주어진 문장은 담화 표지 'In contrast'로 시작하며, 대명사 'them'이 앞 문장에 등장한 여성(women)을 가리키고 있다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 여성을 특정 방식으로 묘사하는 내용이 마무리되어야 하고, 뒤에는 그와 대조되는 묘사 방식의 구체적인 설명 또는 다른 주제로의 전환이 이어져야 한다. ④ 바로 앞 문장인 'Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects.'는 당대 다른 화가들이 여성을 정물화의 소재로 묘사했다는 내용을 제시하고 있으며, 주어진 문장의 'In contrast'는 바로 이 내용과 대조를 이루어 Ancher가 여성을 일상적인 활동의 능동적 참여자로 표현했음을 드러낸다. ④ 이후 문장은 빛과 색채 탐구로 주제가 전환되므로, 여성 묘사 방식의 대조가 마무리되는 ④ 자리에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
Bill Traylor was born into slavery in 1853 on an Alabama plantation, and even after he became a freeman, he remained on the same land working as a farm laborer to support his large family. After spending decades in rural areas, he moved to the city of Montgomery around 1928, where he began a remarkable second life as an artist in his eighties. Living on the streets, Traylor drew on discarded cardboard to depict his memories of the past and the changing African American culture, creating a unique visual language despite being illiterate. His work was recognized and saved by local artist Charles Shannon, and although Traylor died in 1949, a major exhibition in 1982 finally brought his artistic genius to the world's attention.

Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I'm Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you're going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let's explore each artist's life and artwork. The first artist we're going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we're going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art.

Now let's take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother's encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman's Wife. 그녀는 또한 빛과 색을 능숙하게 탐구하면서, 덴마크의 풍성한 인 상주의 운동에 기여했다. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day.

Now let's take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother's encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman's Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day. Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in appreciating these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.
ⓐfeature: to not include something or someone
ⓑencourage: to give someone support or confidence to do something
ⓒpersist: to keep doing something even when it is difficult
ⓓdiffer: to be unlike someone or something else
ⓔamaze: to make someone feel very surprised and impressed
solution: ① 제시된 풀이 'to not include something or someone(무언가나 누군가를 포함하지 않다)'은 feature(특징으로 포함하다)의 뜻과 반대이다. feature의 올바른 풀이는 'to include someone or something as an important part(중요한 부분으로 포함하다)'이다. ② encourage(격려하다): 무언가를 할 수 있도록 지지나 자신감을 주다 ③ persist(지속하다): 어렵더라도 계속해서 무언가를 하다 ④ differ(다르다): 다른 사람이나 사물과 같지 않다 ⑤ amaze(놀라게 하다): 누군가를 매우 놀랍고 인상적으로 느끼게 만들다

밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 틀린 것은?
From Shadows to Spotlights Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.
solution: 본문에서 discrimination은 he still had to face racial discrimination과 같이 사용되어 인종 때문에 부당한 대우를 받는 것을 의미한다. 따라서 discrimination은 “차별”이라는 뜻이어야 한다. 하지만 ③의 영영 풀이인 fair treatment of people regardless of their background는 “배경과 관계없이 사람들을 공정하게 대우하는 것”이라는 의미이므로 원래 뜻과 반대되어 틀린 설명이다. 반면 나머지는 모두 올바른 영영 풀이이다. ① docent : 박물관이나 미술관에서 관람객을 안내하는 사람 → ‘전시 안내인’ ② slavery : 다른 사람에게 소유되어 강제로 일해야 하는 상태 → ‘노예 제도, 노예 상태’ ④ wage : 노동이나 서비스의 대가로 지급되는 돈 → ‘임금’ ⑤ portray : 예술 작품이나 글에서 사람이나 사물을 묘사하다 → ‘묘사하다’
choices: docent : a person who guides visitors in a museum or art gallery
slavery : the condition of being owned and forced to work by another person
discrimination : fair treatment of people regardless of their background
wage : money paid to workers for their labor or services
portray : to show or describe someone or something in a work of art or writing

다음 글을 통해 추론할 수 있는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.
solution: ③ docent는 '가르치다'라는 뜻의 라틴어에서, curator는 '돌보다'라는 뜻의 라틴어에서 유래했다고 했으므로, 각 단어의 어원이 두 역할의 서로 다른 초점, 즉 '가르침 vs 관리'를 반영한다는 것을 추론할 수 있다. ① 도슨트가 고급 학위를 요구받는다는 내용은 언급되지 않았으며, 고급 학위는 큐레이터에게 기대되는 자격이므로 적절하지 않다. ② 전시 작품을 선정하고 배치하는 것은 도슨트가 아니라 큐레이터의 역할이므로 적절하지 않다. ④ 큐레이터가 자원봉사자로 도슨트를 돕는다는 내용은 본문과 반대되며, 자원봉사자는 도슨트를 가리킨다. ⑤ 도슨트는 '발표, 의사소통 기술 훈련'을, 큐레이터는 '고급 학위'를 요구받으므로 동일한 훈련을 받는다는 내용은 적절하지 않다. 미래엔(김) 3과 실전 모의고사 1회차

The word origins of docent and curator reflect the different focus of each role.
Curators mainly work as volunteers who assist docents during museum tours.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis' paintings create a magical quality, like (A)that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

Bill Traylor is a renowned folk artist who captured the key historical changes in American society. His works are especially valuable considering his passion for art despite many challenges in life. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination. Later, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama at the age of 70 to work at a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old that he quit working and turned to drawing to express his life experiences. In his paintings, Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog, Traylor reveals his strong fear of dogs, depicting them as a threatening beast. Because dogs had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves, his fear reflects his early life as a slave. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Through paintings, Traylor . As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art.

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.
solution: ② 이 글은 도슨트와 큐레이터라는 두 역할이 비슷해 보이지만 실제로는 어원, 주요 역할, 신분과 자격 면에서 뚜렷이 다르다는 것을 설명하고 있으므로 ②가 가장 적절하다. ① 유럽 미술관의 역사적 기원에 관한 내용은 언급되지 않았다. ③ 현대 미술관이 겪는 재정적 어려움은 본문과 무관하다. ④ 박물관 취업을 위한 정규 교육의 필요성 자체가 아니라, 큐레이터에게 기대되는 자격 중 하나로만 언급되었으나, 전체를 포괄하는 주제가 되기에는 알맞지 않다. ⑤ 개인 소장품을 위한 작품 선정 과정은 본문에서 다루지 않았다.

solution: ⓐ '미술관에 가본 적이 있다면(have ever been)'이라는 과거의 경험을 바탕으로 한 추측을 나타내므로, 조동사 may 뒤에 완료형인 「have + 과거분사」를 써서 '~마주쳤을지도 모른다'라는 의미를 완성하는 것이 알맞다. ⓑ 「with + 명사 + 분사」 형태의 부대상황(동시동작) 구문이다. 도슨트라는 단어가 라틴어에서 '유래하는' 능동의 의미를 지니므로 현재분사(-ing) 형태가 알맞다. ⓒ 전시회에 '다뤄지는(포함되는)' 예술가들이라는 수동의 의미로 앞에 있는 명사(artists)를 뒤에서 수식해야 하므로 과거분사 형태가 알맞다. ⓓ 뒤에 오는 명사 교육(training)을 수식하며, '전문화된'이라는 수동 및 완료의 의미를 지니므로 과거분사 형태가 알맞다. ⓔ 큐레이터들이 고학력을 '소지할 것으로(to possess) 기대된다(are expected)'는 문맥이다. 주어가 수동의 입장이므로 수동태(be expected)를 쓰고, 그 뒤에 to부정사를 연결한 형태가 알맞다. 등위접속사 and에 의해 앞의 동사(are employed)와 병렬 구조를 이루므로 be동사는 are가 된다.

Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day. Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in appreciating these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.
solution: ⑤ Ancher는 빛과 색채를 능숙하게 탐구하여 덴마크의 풍성한 인상주의 운동에 기여했다고만 했으므로, 그녀가 덴마크에 인상주의를 처음 도입한 화가라는 내용은 추론할 수 없다. ① 이 전시의 마지막 화가로 Ancher를 소개하고 이어서 투어를 마무리하는 인사를 하므로, 그녀의 작품이 전시의 마지막 부분에 소개되었다고 추론할 수 있다. ② 파리 유학은 당시 여성에게 드문 일이었고 어머니의 격려 덕분에 이러한 기회를 활용할 수 있었다고 했으므로, 어머니가 당시 여성이 드물게 걷던 교육의 길을 지지했다고 추론할 수 있다. ③ 기혼 여성은 집안일에만 전념해야 한다는 사회적 압력에 반대하며 결혼 후에도 그림을 계속 그렸다고 했으므로, 그녀의 행보가 사회적 기대에 어긋났다고 추론할 수 있다. ④ 당대 다른 화가들이 여성을 정물처럼 그린 것과 달리 Ancher는 일상 업무에 적극적으로 참여하는 모습으로 그렸다고 했으므로, 여성을 사물이 아닌 일하는 사람으로 표현했다고 추론할 수 있다.

Ancher's mother supported an educational path that few women of her era took.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.
solution: ④ Traylor는 개들이 농장에서 노예를 감시하고 사냥하는 데 자주 이용되었기 때문에 개를 몹시 두려워했다고 했으므로 일치한다. ① Isabel Williams는 전시회의 도슨트로 소개되었을 뿐 작품을 그렸다는 내용은 없으므로 일치하지 않는다. ② Traylor가 Montgomery로 이주한 것은 약 70세 때였으므로 일치하지 않는다. ③ Traylor는 85세에 몸이 너무 아파 일할 수 없게 되어서야 그림을 시작했으므로 정반대이다. ⑤ Man with Umbrella는 Traylor가 Montgomery 거리에서 실제로 관찰한 아프리카계 미국인들의 자유로운 삶을 그린 것이지 바라던 자유를 그린 것이 아니므로 일치하지 않는다.

Bill Traylor started drawing while he was still healthy enough to keep working.

Man with Umbrella depicts the freedom that African Americans hoped to have someday.

(C) 주어진 문장 뒤에는 시간의 흐름에 따라 남북전쟁 이후 자유인이 되었으나 70세까지 고된 삶을 살았고, 85세가 되어서야 비로소 삶의 경험을 표현하기 위해 '그림 그리기 (drawing)에 눈을 돌렸다'는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. (A) (C)의 마지막 부분에서 그가 그림을 그리기 시작했다는 내용(turned to drawing)을 바탕으로, "Now, ~ (이제, 그의 그림들 중 일부를 살펴보자)"라며 구체적인 초기 작품들(개에 대한 두려움을 표현한 그림들)을 소개하는 (A)가 이어져야 한다. (B) 마지막으로, 연결어 "In contrast(대조적으로)"를 사용하여 (A)의 두려움을 표현한 그림들과 대비되는 '자유로운 삶'을 묘사한 작품(Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella)을 소개하고, 그의 예술적 의의를 평가하며 글을 마무리하는 (B)가 오는 것이 논리적이다. 따라서 가장 적절한 글의 순서는 ④가 가장 알맞다.

solution: ⓐ valuing → valued 5형식 동사 made의 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어인 'their work'가 높이 평가 '받는' 수동의 관계이다. 따라서 현재분사 valuing을 과거분사 valued로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ to work → working 'spend + 시간 + -ing'는 '~하면서 시간을 보내다'라는 의미의 구문으로, spend 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 한다. 따라서 to부정사 to work를 동명사 working으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ used → been used 주어 they가 가리키는 dogs는 노예를 감시하고 사냥하는 데 '이용된' 대상이므로 수동태가 되어야 한다. 과거완료 수동태인 'had been p.p.'의 형태가 되도록 used를 been used로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ 외의 밑줄은 다음과 같은 이유로 옳다. ⓒ 'It wasn't until ~ that ...'은 '~하고 나서야 비로소 … 했다'라는 의미의 강조 구문이므로 that이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 Traylor가 단순한 형태와 색을 직접 사용하는 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사 Using이 올바르게 쓰였다.

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a ⓐrenowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as ⓑ distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To ⓒmake a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often
ⓓdepicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings ⓔgradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.
solution: ① 제시된 풀이 '많은 사람들에게 알려지거나 인정받지 못한'은 renowned(유명한)의 뜻과 반대이다. renowned의 올바른 풀이는 'known and admired by many people(많은 사람들에게 알려지고 존경받는)'이다. 따라서 ①이 정답이다. ② distorted(뒤틀린, 비뚤어진): 비틀어지거나 정상적인 모양에서 바뀐 ③ make a living(생계를 꾸리다): 살아가는 데 필요한 돈을 벌다 ④ depict(묘사하다): 그림이나 회화 속에 누군가나 무언가를 보여 주다 ⑤ gradually(점차): 일정 기간에 걸쳐 천천히 미래엔(김) 3과 실전 모의고사 3회차

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

The first artist we're going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we're going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art.
solution: ① 남북전쟁 이후 자유인이 되었음에도 여전히 인종 차별에 직면했다고 언급되어 있으므로, 남북전쟁이 인종 차별의 완전한 종식을 가져왔다는 내용은 추론할 수 없다. ② 자신이 두려워했던 개, 관찰했던 사람들을 그렸으므로 개인적 경험이 작품 주제에 영향을 미쳤음을 추론할 수 있다. ③ 몽고메리 거리에서 관찰한 흑인들의 자유로운 삶을 묘사했다는 부분에서 추론할 수 있다. ④ 젊은 시절 농장과 공장에서 일했고 85세에 그림을 시작했으므로 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ 너무 병들어 일할 수 없게 된 것이 그림을 그리게 된 계기가 되었으므로 추론할 수 있다. 미래엔(김) 3과 실전 모의고사 3회차

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical ⓐweaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis ⓑcontinued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an ⓒoriginal, innovative style. Although her physical limitations ⓓexpanded her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a ⓔmagical quality, like that of a fairy tale.

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, . In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. 그 결과, 그는 현재 미국 민속 예술에서 중요한 인물로 여겨진다.
4회차 실전 모의고사
조건 1. 수동태를 사용할 것
2. (American folk art, now, important figure, as a result, consider)를 모두 포함할 것
3. 필요 시 어형을 변화시킬 것
→
answer: As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.
solution: 그 결과'라는 의미의 연결어 'as a result'를 문장 맨 앞에 쓰고 쉼표로 구분한 뒤, 주어 'he'를 쓴다. '~로 여겨지다'는 동사 'consider'의 수동태로 표현해야 하므로 수동태 조건에 따라 be동사 'is'와 과거분사 'considered'를 추가하여 'he's now considered'로 쓰며, '현재'를 뜻하는 부사 'now'는 be동사와 과거분사 사이에 둔다. 'consider A B' 구문이 수동태로 바뀌면서 목적격보어 'an important figure'가 'considered' 바로 뒤에 오므로, 박스의 'important figure' 앞에 관사 'an'을 추가한다. 마지막으로 '미국 민속 예술에서'는 전치사 'in'을 추가하여 'in American folk art'로 완성한다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this exhibition:
Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day. Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in appreciating these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience. Docent vs. Curator

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
A kangaroo's tail, ⓐthat is made up of over twenty vertebrae, acts as a powerful muscle for balance and movement. The tail works almost like a fifth leg ⓑso that the kangaroo can hop, turn, and even fight without losing stability. When a kangaroo stands still, its tail ⓒsupports most of its body weight while the legs rest. During a fight, a kangaroo often begins ⓓkicking its opponent with both hind legs while balancing on its tail. Before hopping away, the kangaroo tucks its front legs close to its chest to protect ⓔthem from injury. *vertebrae: 척추뼈
solution: ①ⓐ이 정답이다. 'A kangaroo's tail, that is made up of over twenty vertebrae'에서 콤마 뒤의 계속적 용법 관계대명사로는 'that'을 쓸 수 없으므로 'which'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ 'so that'은 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어져 목적이나 결과를 나타내는 접속사로 올바르다. ⓒ 주어 'its tail'이 단수이므로 단수동사 'supports'가 알맞다. ⓓ 'begin + -ing' 구조에서 'kicking'이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 'them'은 앞의 복수명사 'front legs'를 가리키는 대명사로 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

A bat's brain processes returning echoes ⓐso that it can determine the exact distance and shape of nearby objects in total darkness. As soon as a bat begins flying, it starts ⓑemitting a rapid series of high-pitched clicks. Each click
ⓒtravels outward until it hits an object and bounces back to the bat's ears. These returning signals, ⓓthat are analyzed within milliseconds, allow the bat to build a detailed map of its surroundings. A bat also uses its wings to catch insects, tucking them close to its body to keep
ⓔthem from escaping. *echo: 반향(음)
solution: ④ⓓ가 정답이다. 'These returning signals, that are analyzed within milliseconds'에서 콤마 뒤의 계속적 용법 관계대명사로는 'that'을 쓸 수 없으므로 'which'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 'so that'은 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어져 목적이나 결과를 나타내는 접속사로 올바르다. ⓑ 'start + -ing' 구조에서 'emitting'이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 'Each click'은 단수 주어이므로 단수동사 'travels'가 알맞다. ⓔ 'them'은 앞의 복수명사 'insects'를 가리키는 대명사로 적절하다. 미래엔(김) 3과 문법 정복 실전

The majority of the refrigerators we have at home or in restaurants (A)[is / are] actually prone to picking up strong odors from food. They absorb smells easily, and most compartments aren't very well sealed. Spraying air freshener isn't a true solution, (B)[although / despite] what many advertisements claim. It can affect both the taste of stored food and your health, and the smell returns immediately anyway. A clever way to solve the odor problem is to place a small bowl with baking soda and charcoal and (C)[places / place] it inside the fridge or near the vents. The odor fades slowly through absorption — much less quickly than it will through the food itself — and keeps a little more freshness in the air around your fridge.
solution: (A)의 주어는 'The majority of the refrigerators'이며, 'majority of + 복수명사'는 복수 취급하므로 'are'가 알맞다. (B)의 'what many advertisements claim'은 명사절이므로 전치사 'despite'가 알맞다. (C)는 'to place ~ and place ~'의 병렬 구조이므로 동사원형 'place'가 알맞다. 따라서 정답은 ①이다.

다음을 읽고, 어법상 틀린 부분을 한 군데 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
Urban noise pollution has had positive influences on the way people adapt to city life and stay alert. However, although constant noise seems to be a normal part of city living, it is actually reducing people's ability to focus. The more time people spend in noisy environments, the less concentration they have. Many researchers now believe that noise pollution can lead to a number of cognitive problems. In fact, a recent study showed that traffic noise raises cortisol levels, that explains why people who live in noisy areas experience significant levels of stress, fatigue, and other cognitive issues.
→
solution: 콤마 다음에 와서 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 삼아 부가적 정보를 제공하는 비제한적 관계대명사 자리에는 that이 올 수 없고 which를 써야 한다. 'raises cortisol levels, that explains why'의 that을 which로 고쳐야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
어법상 틀린 것을 모두 골라 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
ⓐThis is all that the manager expects from us.
ⓑThe brush with that she painted the picture is broken.
ⓒHe is the only player that scored a goal today.
ⓓTell that you learned in class.
ⓔDid you notice the girl and her parrot that were singing on stage?
→
→
answer: ⓑ with that → with which, ⓓ Tell that → Tell what
solution: ⓑ는 관계대명사 that이 전치사 바로 뒤에 올 수 없으므로 with that을 with which로 고쳐야 한다. (The brush with which she painted the picture is broken.) ⓓ는 선행사 없이 '~하는 것'이라는 의미로 관계대명사 that을 명사절처럼 쓴 오류로, that을 what으로 고쳐야 한다. (Tell what you learned in class.) ⓐ은 all이 선행사일 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 자연스러우므로 옳다. ⓒ은 the only가 선행사를 수식할 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 적절하므로 옳다. ⓔ는 선행사가 사람(girl)과 동물(parrot)이 함께 있을 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 자연스러우므로 옳다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 문장 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
solution: ④ because of he was feeling sick → because he was feeling sick because of는 전치사이므로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 한다. 뒤에 주어와 동사로 이루어진 절이 이어지므로 접속사 because가 알맞다. ① Even if는 ‘비록 ~일지라도’라는 양보의 접속사로 절을 이끄므로 알맞다. ② As ~, so + 동사 + 주어의 도치 구조로 알맞다. ③ where는 place를 선행사로 하며 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지므로 알맞다. ⑤ Not until이 문두에 나오면서 주어와 동사가 도치된 구조로 알맞다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

Internet addiction often begins as a result of a stressful experience. Common stressful experiences are loneliness, anxiety (A)[due to / since] exams, or dissatisfaction with real-life relationships. People who worry about being left out may be more likely to develop internet addiction. Teenagers are particularly vulnerable,
(B)[because / because of] the pressure at this time in life to stay connected and to keep up with friends online. Added to this is the pressure (C)[on / of] teenagers from social media to gain followers, to post frequently, to maintain an image and to meet peers' expectations. * internet addiction 인터넷 중독 / vulnerable (위험 등에) 노 출되어 있는
solution: (A) 뒤에 명사구(exams)가 이어지므로 전치사 due to가 적절하다. since는 뒤에 절이 와야 한다. (B) 뒤에 명사구(the pressure ~)가 이어지므로 전치사구 because of가 적절하다. because는 뒤에 절이 와야 한다. (C) 'pressure on 사람' 형태의 어구이므로 on이 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤이다.

The platypus is one of the most unusual mammals in the world. Its name was derived from the Greek words platus and pous, (A)[that / which] mean "flat foot," referring to its webbed feet. The platypus can detect electrical signals from prey underwater, (B)[although / despite] it doesn't have very good eyesight. Platypuses belong to a group of mammals called monotremes, and that name refers to mammals that lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young. To put it more concretely, they are egg-laying mammals (C)[like / alike] echidnas. Also, they belong to the family Ornithorhynchidae. Other than platypuses, there are no other living members of that family. *monotreme 단공류 **Ornithorhynchidae 오리너구리과
solution: (A) 콤마 뒤에서 앞의 명사(the Greek words platus and pous)를 계속적으로 설명하는 관계대명사 자리이므로 that이 아닌 which가 와야 한다. (B) 뒤에 '주어+동사'로 이루어진 절(it doesn't have very good eyesight)이 이어지므로 접속사 although가 필요하다. despite는 전치사로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 한다. (C) 뒤에 명사(echidnas)가 이어지므로 전치사 like가 적절하다. alike는 명사를 수식하는 자리에 쓰일 수 없다. 따라서 정답은 ① which - although - like이다. 미래엔(김) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

that - despite - alike
which - despite - like
that - although - alike

body: 다음 중 문장 전환이 바르지 않은 것은?
solution: ⑤는 앞 문장의 they가 refused의 주어 역할을 하므로 목적격 whom이 아니라 주격 관계대명사 who를 써야 한다. 따라서 ‘whom refused my apology’를 ‘who refused my apology’로 고쳐야 한다. ①은 the thing that을 what으로, ②는 anyone whom을 whomever로, ③은 no matter where를 wherever로, ④는 there를 관계부사 where로 바꾼 표현으로 모두 옳다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전
choices: The thing that he most desires is freedom. →What he most desires is freedom.
You can invite anyone whom you admire to the party. →You can invite whomever you admire to the party.
No matter where she hides, her dog finds her. →Wherever she hides, her dog finds her.
We entered the garden, and there we found a hidden fountain. →We entered the garden, where we found a hidden fountain.
I apologized my classmates, but they refused my apology. →I apologized my classmates, whom refused my apology.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
In traditional manufacturing plants, the difference in efficiency between experienced workers and new employees ⓐis closely linked to the level of hands-on training received. As manufacturing
ⓑbecomes less reliant on manual dexterity, the efficiency gap between the two groups ⓒmight expect to widen. However, this is far from being so. ⓓIt is usually the veterans who train newcomers on new machinery while the newcomers themselves struggle to keep pace.
ⓔNew automated systems having been installed, there is less need for manual dexterity. Nevertheless, the efficiency gap tends to widen
ⓕbecause of newcomers struggle with the unfamiliar technology. Thus, in the course of automation, new employees' efficiency remains
ⓖunchanged compared to veterans'.
solution: 정답은 ①이다. ⓒ '주어인 the efficiency gap'은 스스로 기대하는 행위의 주체가 아니므로 'might expect to widen'이 아니라 'might be expected to widen'과 같이 수동태로 써야 한다. ⓕ 'because of'는 전치사이므로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 하는데, 'newcomers struggle'이라는 주어+동사로 이루어진 절이 왔으므로 어법상 틀리다. 'because newcomers struggle'(because+절) 또는 'because of newcomers' struggle'(because of+명사)로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ는 'is closely linked'로 주어와 수 일치가 올바르다. ⓑ는 'becomes less reliant'로 현재시제와 형용사 보어가 적절하다. ⓓ는 'It is usually the veterans who train'으로 강조구문 (cleft sentence)이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ는 'New automated systems having been installed'로 완료 수동 분사구문이 적절히 쓰였다. ⓖ는 'unchanged compared'로 형용사와 분사의 결합이 자연스럽다.

body:

Octopuses have a remarkable ability to disappear into their surroundings, and they use this skill to avoid predators. So if you're an octopus, you need to blend in quickly to survive. When (A)[hiding / hidden] itself among rocks and coral, the octopus will often change its skin texture and color within seconds, matching the pattern of its environment almost perfectly. The octopus's flexible body already gives it an advantage over predators, which have a hard time spotting movement in cluttered reefs. But predators are persistent. Marine biologists who studied octopuses in aquariums reported seeing them do something quite surprising (B)[improved / to improve] their chances of escaping notice. According to these studies, as the octopus settles into a hiding spot, it sometimes flattens its body against the surface,
(C)[which / what] allows it to reduce its shadow. Apparently, the octopus minimizes its outline.
solution: (A) 문어가 스스로 몸을 숨기는 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 hiding이 적절하다. hidden은 수동의 의미가 되어 문맥에 맞지 않는다. (B) '눈에 띄지 않을 가능성을 높이기 위해'라는 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 to improve가 적절하다. (C) 앞 문장 전체 내용을 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. what은 선행사를 가질 수 없으므로 어법상 틀리다. 따라서 정답은 ④이다.

With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides ⓑwhich lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy
ⓒto share their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way ⓓwhich captivates the audience. Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. ⓐBorn in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia,
ⓑwhich she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, ⓒgenerated an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows ⓓdecorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later ⓔmaking into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art. ( ) _____ → ( ) _____ → ( ) _____ → 실전 학습
answer: ⓑ which → where, ⓒ generated → generating, ⓔ making → made
solution: ⓑ which → where 뒤에 이어지는 절 'she met her future husband, Everett Lewis'는 주어와 목적어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이다. 따라서 장소를 나타내는 선행사 'Digby, Nova Scotia'를 받으려면 관계대명사 which가 아니라 관계부사 where를 써야 한다. ⓒ generated → generating 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어 'Her artwork'이다. 작품이 독창적이고 혁신적인 스타일을 직접 만들어 낸다는 능동의 의미이고, 뒤에 목적어 'an original, innovative style'도 있다. 따라서 과거분사 generated를 현재분사 generating으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ making → made 주어 'her story'는 책과 영화로 '만들어지는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미이다. 따라서 'was later making'을 수동태 'was later made'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 주절의 주어 Lewis가 '태어난' 것이므로 수동의 의미이다. 따라서 과거분사로 시작하는 분사구문 Born이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ 소들이 '장식된' 대상이므로 명사 cows를 앞에서 수식하는 과거분사 decorated가 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly ⓐvalued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life ⓑworking on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, ⓒwhich he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often
ⓓbeen used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. ⓔUsing simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.
solution: ③ which → where 선행사 'the city of Montgomery, Alabama' 뒤에 오는 'he found a job in a factory'는 주어와 목적어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이다. 따라서 관계대명사 which는 쓸 수 없고, 장소를 나타내는 관계부사 where를 써야 한다. where는 in which로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다. 따라서 ③이 정답이다. ① 'make+목적어+목적격보어' 구문에서 목적어 'their work'는 '가치 있게 평가되는' 대상이다. 따라서 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 valued가 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 'spend+시간+-ing' 구문으로 '~하면서 시간을 보내다'라는 의미이므로 working이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 주어 they가 가리키는 개들은 농장에서 '이용된' 대상이다. 또한 공포를 갖게 된 시점보다 앞선 일이므로 과거완료 수동태 had been used가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 주절의 주어 Traylor가 단순한 형태와 색을 직접 '사용하는' 주체이므로, 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사로 시작하는 분사구문 Using이 올바르게 쓰였다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

solution: ⓐ '미술관에 가본 적이 있다면(have ever been)'이라는 과거의 경험을 바탕으로 한 추측을 나타내므로, 조동사 may 뒤에 완료형인 「have + 과거분사」를 써서 '~마주쳤을지도 모른다'라는 의미를 완성하는 것이 알맞다. ⓑ 「with + 명사 + 분사」 형태의 부대상황(동시동작) 구문이다. 도슨트라는 단어가 라틴어에서 '유래하는' 능동의 의미를 지니므로 현재분사(-ing) 형태가 알맞다. ⓒ 전시회에 '다뤄지는(포함되는)' 예술가들이라는 수동의 의미로 앞에 있는 명사(artists)를 뒤에서 수식해야 하므로 과거분사 형태가 알맞다. ⓓ 뒤에 오는 명사 교육(training)을 수식하며, '전문화된'이라는 수동 및 완료의 의미를 지니므로 과거분사 형태가 알맞다. ⓔ 큐레이터들이 고학력을 '소지할 것으로(to possess) 기대된다(are expected)'는 문맥이다. 주어가 수동의 입장이므로 수동태(be expected)를 쓰고, 그 뒤에 to부정사를 연결한 형태가 알맞다. 등위접속사 and에 의해 앞의 동사(are employed)와 병렬 구조를 이루므로 be동사는 are가 된다.

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.

solution: 밑줄 친 부분은 부사 ever와 함께 쓰여 과거부터 현재까지 '~ 에 가본 적이 있다'라는 의미를 나타내는 현재완료의 경험 용법이다. ⓑ 과거에 여권을 잃어버려서 현재 가지고 있지 않다는 과거 동작의 결과를 나타내므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓓ 부사 already(이미)와 함께 쓰여 동작이 이미 끝났음을 의미하는 완료 용법이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓔ 기간을 나타내는 전치사 for(~동안)와 함께 쓰여 과거부터 지금까지 동작이나 상태가 이어지는 계속 용법이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓐ 부사 never(결코 ~해 본 적 없다)와 함께 쓰여 과거의 경험을 나타내므로 쓰임이 같다. ⓒ 부사 ever(~해 본 적이)와 함께 쓰여 과거의 경험을 묻고 있으므로 쓰임이 같다. ⓕ 횟수를 나타내는 부사구 three times(세 번)와 함께 쓰여 과거의 경험을 나타내므로 쓰임이 같다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 어법 설명으로 가장 알맞 은 것은?
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known ⓐfor her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia,
ⓑwhere she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were ⓒboth limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and ⓓwas later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and ⓔbecame an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.
solution: ⓓ 등위접속사 and에 의해 앞의 동사(inspired)와 병렬 구조를 이루고 있다. 주어인 '그녀의 이야기(her story)'가 책과 영화로 '제작되는' 수동의 입장이므로 과거형 수동태 (was made)로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓐ 그림 '때문에' 유명해진 것이므로 이유나 업적을 나타내는 전치사 for(~로 유명한)가 알맞다: as를 쓰면 '~로서 알려지다'라는 신분이나 자격이 되어 문맥상 어색하다. ⓑ 선행사(장소) 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 관계부사 where로 쓴 것이 알맞다. : which 뒤에는 주어나 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장이 와야 한다. ⓒ 문맥상 신체적 약점이 아니라, 바로 앞에 있는 주어인 '그녀의 재능과 상상력(her talent and imagination)' 두 가지 모두를 가리키는 표현이다. ⓔ 등위접속사 and에 의해 앞의 과거형 동사(expressed)와 병렬 구조를 이루어 주어(Maud Lewis)의 두 번째 동작을 나타내므로 과거형 동사 became이 알맞다.

choices: ⓐ: '유명한 예술가로서'라는 자격을 나타내므로 전치사 as로 고쳐야 한다.
ⓑ: 뒤에 주어, 동사, 목적어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어지므로 목 적격 관계대명사 which로 고쳐야 한다.
ⓒ: 문맥상 앞에 나온 두 가지 신체적 약점을 가리키는 대명사로 쓰였 다.
ⓓ: 주어인 그녀의 이야기가 책과 영화로 '만들어진' 수동의 관계이므 로 수동태로 쓰인 것이 알맞다.
ⓔ: 문장의 주어에 대한 부연 설명을 하는 분사구문 자리이므로 becoming으로 고쳐야 한다. 실전 학습 교과서 문법 정복

다음 글의 밑줄 친 observing과 쓰임이 같은 문장을 <보 기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day. 실전 학습
보기 ⓐWalking along the street, I met an old friend.
ⓑHis favorite hobby is playing the piano in his free time.
ⓒWhile waiting for the bus, she fell asleep on the bench.
ⓓThank you for inviting me to your birthday party.
ⓔNot knowing what to say, he just stood there quietly.
ⓕKeeping a diary in English is not as easy as it sounds.
solution: 밑줄 친 부분은 접속사(When)의 의미를 명확하게 하기 위해 생략하지 않고 남겨둔 현재분사(분사구문)로 쓰였다. 주절의 주어(you)가 그림을 직접 '관찰할 때'라는 능동의 의미를 나타낸다. ⓐ '거리를 걷다가'라는 의미로 시간, 동시동작 등을 나타내는 분사구문이므로 알맞다. ⓒ 접속사 While을 생략하지 않은 분사구문으로, 주어(she) 가 버스를 '기다리는 동안'이라는 능동의 의미를 나타내므로 알맞다. ⓔ '무엇을 말해야 할지 몰라서'라는 이유를 나타내는 분사구문의 부정형이므로 알맞다. ⓑ be동사 뒤에서 주어(hobby)를 보충 설명하는 주격 보어로 쓰여 '~하는 것'으로 해석되므로 동명사이다. ⓓ 전치사 for의 목적어로 쓰여 '초대해 준 것'으로 해석되는 동명사로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓕ 문장의 맨 앞에서 주어로 쓰여 '일기를 쓰는 것은'으로 해석되는 동명사로 쓰임이 다르다.

solution: ⓐ renown → renowned 뒤에 오는 명사(artist)를 수식하여 '유명한 예술가'라는 뜻이 되어야 하므로, 명사형인 renown(명성)이 아니라 형용사/ 과거분사 형태인 renowned가 알맞다. ⓔ stand → standing '장식된 소들이 꽃밭에 서 있는(standing) 것을 보여준다'는 문맥이다. 앞에 쓰인 동사 shows는 지각동사나 사역동사가 아니므로 동사원형을 쓸 수 없다. 명사(decorated cows)의 상태를 보충 설명하며 능동과 진행의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 standing으로 고쳐야 알맞다. ⓑ 분사구문의 주어(Lewis)가 '태어난' 수동의 입장이므로 과거분사(Born)로 시작하는 것이 알맞다. ⓒ 선행사가 장소(Digby, Nova Scotia)일 때 보통 관계부사 where(또는 in which)를 쓰지만, 이 문장에서는 뒤에 전치사 in이 남아있으므로 전치사의 목적어 역할을 하는 목적격 관계대명사 which를 쓴 것이 문법적으로 알맞다. ⓓ generating주절의 주어(Her artwork)가 독창적인 스타일을 직접 '만들어내면서'라는 능동의 의미를 지닌 분사구문이므로 현재분사(-ing) 형태가 알맞다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 어법 설명으로 옳지 않은것은?
Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists ⓐwho never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, ⓑworking for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, ⓒwhere he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to
ⓓdrawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now ⓔconsidered an important figure in American folk art.
solution: ⓓ drawing은 to부정사가 아니라 전치사 to의 목적어 역할을 하는 '동명사'이므로 설명이 틀리다. 앞에 쓰인 'turn to + 명사/동명사'는 '~에 의존하다, ~로 눈을 돌리다'라는 뜻의 숙어이다. 이때 to는 방향을 나타내는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동사원형이 아닌 동명사가 오는 것이 알맞다. ⓐ 선행사 'artists' 뒤에 바로 동사가 이어지므로 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사로 알맞다. ⓑ '주어 he'와 일하다의 관계가 직접 수행하는 능동이므로 현재분사를 사용한 분사구문으로 알맞다. ⓒ 선행사 'the city of Montgomery, Alabama'라는 장소 뒤에서 쉼표(,)와 함께 쓰였고, 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 관계부사 where가 알맞다. ⓔ 'consider A B (A를 B로 여기다)' 구문에서 목적어(A)가 주어 자리로 나간 수동태가 되었고, 목적격 보어인 명사가 뒤에 그대로 남은 형태이므로 알맞다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전
choices: ⓐ: 선행사 artists 를 수식하며, 이어지는 절 안에서 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사이다.
ⓑ: 주절의 주어 he가 농장에서 직접 일한다는 능동의 의미 를 나타내는 분사구문이다.
ⓒ: 선행사인 장소를 부연 설명하며, 뒤에 주어와 목적어를 갖춘 완전한 절을 이끄는 계속적 용법의 관계부사이다.
ⓓ: '그림을 그리기 위하여'라는 목적의 의미를 나타내는 to 부정사의 부사적 용법으로 쓰였다.
ⓔ: 5형식 동사 consider가 수동태로 쓰여 뒤에 목적격 보 어인 명사 an important figure가 남은 형태이다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may ⓐappear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides ⓑwho lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists ⓒfeatured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way ⓓwhich captivates the audience. Curators are typically
ⓔemploying by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.
solution: ⑤ employing by → employed by 'Curators are typically employing by museums'에서 큐레이터들은 박물관에 '고용되는' 대상이므로 수동 관계가 성립한다. 따라서 현재분사 employing이 아닌 과거분사 employed를 써서 'are typically employed by museums'라고 해야 한다. 능동(현재분사)과 수동(과거분사) 의 형태를 혼동한 오류이다. 따라서 ⑤가 정답이다. ① 조동사 may 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 appear가 올바르게 쓰였다. 또한 appear는 보어로 형용사(similar)를 취하는 연결동사로서 적절하다. ② 선행사 guides는 사람을 가리키므로, 주격 관계대명사 who가 올바르게 쓰였다. who lead museum tours는 guides를 수식하는 관계절이다. ③ artworks and artists를 수식하는 분사로, 이들은 전시회에 '전시되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 featured가 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 선행사 an engaging way는 사물이므로 관계대명사 which가 올바르게 쓰였으며, 선행사가 단수이므로 동사 captivates도 수 일치가 맞다.

Now let's take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When ⓐobserved her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, ⓑwhich was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother's encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, ⓒwho depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman's Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall ⓓis stunningly portraying. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day. Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in ⓔto appreciate these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.
→

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist
ⓐknown for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia,
ⓑwhere she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, ⓒgenerating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations
ⓓconfining her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis' paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings
ⓔgradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.
solution: ④ confining → confined Although로 시작하는 종속절 'Although her physical limitations confining her to a small cottage'에서 주어는 'her physical limitations'이다. 종속절 안에는 정동사(finite verb)가 반드시 필요한데, confining은 현재분사로 정동사 역할을 할 수 없다. 따라서 과거시제 정동사 confined로 고쳐야 한다. ① 선행사 'a renowned artist'를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사구에서, artist가 '알려진' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 가지는 과거분사 known이 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 선행사 'Digby, Nova Scotia'가 장소를 나타내므로, 관계부사 where가 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ 앞 문장 전체 내용('Her artwork used a mixture...')에 대한 결과를 나타내는 분사구문으로, artwork가 스타일을 능동적으로 만들어 내는 주체이므로 현재분사 generating이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 동사 gained를 수식하는 부사 gradually가 올바르게 쓰였다. 따라서 ④가 정답이다. 미래엔(김) 3과 문법 정복 실전

Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I'm Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you're going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, ⓐdespite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let's explore each artist's life and artwork. 실전 학습 The first artist we're going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S.
in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, ⓑworked for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, ⓒwhere he found a job in a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we're going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs ⓓis expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor ⓔ capturing complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art. _____ , _____ → _____ , _____ →
solution: ⓑ worked → working 'he still had to face racial discrimination' 뒤에 이어지는 구조로, 주어(he)가 저임금으로 일하는 상황을 동시에 나타내는 분사구문이 필요하다. 주어 he가 능동적으로 일하는 것이므로 현재분사 working을 써야 한다. 과거형 동사 worked를 쓰면 문장에 두 개의 정동사(had, worked)가 접속사 없이 병렬되어 문법적으로 옳지 않다. ⓔ capturing → captured 'Using simple shapes and colors' 다음에 오는 주절의 동사 자리이다. 주어 Traylor에 대한 서술어가 필요하므로 정동사 형태인 captured가 와야 한다. 현재분사 capturing을 쓰면 주절에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 성립하지 않는다. ⓐ despite는 전치사로, 뒤에 명사구 'challenges in their lives'를 취하고 있으므로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ where는 선행사 'the city of Montgomery, Alabama'를 받아 장소를 나타내는 관계부사로, 뒤에 완전한 절('he found a job in a factory')이 이어지므로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ 'His fear of dogs'가 주어이고, 두려움이 그림 속에 표현되는 것이므로 수동태 is expressed가 올바르게 쓰였다.

From Shadows to Spotlights Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly ⓐvalued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial ⓑdiscrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to ⓒconceal his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the ⓓoppressed lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an ⓔimportant figure in American folk art.

Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, ⓒinnovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both ⓓlimitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became a ⓔmarginal figure in Canadian folk art.

다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Neuroscience has a long history of exploring treatments for disorders of the nervous system, including the brain and spinal cord. Traditionally, researchers have studied various functions of neural implants, which are medical devices like computer chips that can be implanted in the nervous system. But here's the exciting part: with the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), researchers have begun to integrate AI into neural implants. In this post, we'll examine the incredible benefits of AI-powered neural implants, their amazing potential for the future, and the ethical concerns surrounding them. First, let's explore how this fascinating technology has been applied. The AI-powered neural implant has shown great promise in medical applications, offering solutions to a range of problems. For instance, neural implants are used to treat brain disorders like Parkinson's disease. These implants electrically stimulate targeted regions of the brain at the right time with the help of AI to restore normal brain activity. In addition, paralyzed people can have the ability to walk again with the help of a "digital bridge" between two implants inserted into their brain and spine. When they think about moving their legs, the AI analyzes the brain signals and sends them to their legs through the implants. Similarly, those who have lost their arms can use artificial arms operated by the same mechanism.
solution: ① 글의 도입부에서 "we'll examine the incredible benefits of AI-powered neural implants, their amazing potential for the future, and the ethical concerns surrounding them"이라고 글 전체의 주제를 직접 밝히고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 가장 적절하다. ② 신경과학의 역사는 도입부에 간략히 언급될 뿐, 글 전체의 주제인 AI 기반 신경 임플란트의 혜택과 윤리적 우려를 담지 못한다. ③ 파킨슨병은 AI 신경 임플란트의 적용 사례로 제시된 일화일 뿐, 글의 제목은 아니다. ④ 프라이버시 위협은 본문에 전혀 언급되지 않았다. ⑤ 인공 팔 개발은 본문 말미에 제시된 구체적 사례일 뿐, 글 전체를 포괄하는 제목은 아니다.

다음글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
Before we can fully embrace the era of Al- powered neural implants, many tricky ethical issues should be addressed. The integration of AI technology with the human brain raises concerns about what it means to be human. Our brains are believed to be central to our identity, existence, and value as human beings. However, an over- reliance on technology may delay our natural development and create confusion about whether we are human, Al, or something in between. There's a risk that organizations or hackers could access personal data without permission through Al-connected implants. This means that our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors could be controlled by hackers. There's an additional risk that this technology could lead to even greater social inequality, given that it may not be available to all due to its high cost. Such unequal access to the technology could intensify the division between those who can afford the implants and those who cannot. I hope that we can overcome these challenges through careful consideration of neuroethics. This field highlights the social aspects of neural technology and provides possible answers to what should be considered legal and ethical. I think it is important to establish a prior review process and thoroughly assess the ethical aspects before any kind of brain research is conducted. This will ensure that science and technology progress in accordance with ethical principles.

다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Before we can fully embrace the era of AI- powered neural implants, many tricky ethical issues should be addressed. As the silicon seed takes root in our minds, the defining borders of our own reflection begin to blur. Our brains are believed to be central to our identity, existence, and value as human beings. However, an over- reliance on technology may delay our natural development and create confusion about whether we are human, AI, or something in between. Another critical issue is privacy. There’s a risk that organizations or hackers could access personal data without permission through AI- connected implants. This means that our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors could be controlled by hackers. There’s an additional risk that this technology could lead to even greater social inequality, given that it may not be available to all due to its high cost. Such unequal access to the technology could intensify the division between those who can afford the implants and those who cannot. I hope that we can overcome these challenges through careful consideration of neuroethics. This field highlights the social aspects of neural technology and provides possible answers to what should be considered legal and ethical. I think it is important to establish a prior review process and thoroughly assess the ethical aspects before any kind of brain research is conducted. This will ensure that science and technology progress in accordance with ethical principles. What do you think about this technology? Please share your opinion in the comments section below.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 weaving digital brains into their mechanical parts가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
Artificial limbs, designed to replace natural arms or legs, have a rich history dating back to ancient times. An interesting example is the discovery of a wooden toe on an Egyptian mummy from around 950 B.C. In the 16th century, a German knight known as Götz of the Iron Hand made himself an iron arm with spring-operated fingers so that he could hold his weapon more tightly. During the World Wars of the 20th century, the demand for artificial limbs increased significantly as injured soldiers sought replacements, resulting in remarkable advances in artificial limb technology. Bert Shepard, a soldier who had lost his leg during World War II, made an impressive return to Major League Baseball in 1945 with an artificial leg, showing the potential of artificial limb technology. Today, artificial limbs are weaving digital brains into their mechanical parts. This technological integration enables users to make complex movements and control their artificial limbs with their thoughts. These advancements empower people with limb loss, giving them the freedom and opportunity to lead better lives.
solution: ⑤ 과거 나무나 철로 만들어졌던 단순한 형태의 인공 사지가 20세기를 거쳐 발전해 왔으며, 오늘날에는 사용자가 '생각만으로(with their thoughts)' 복잡한 움직임을 제어할 수 있게 되었다고 글의 후반부에서 설명한다. 따라서 밑줄 친 '기계 부품에 디지털 두뇌를 엮어 넣고 있다'는 표현은 인공 사지에 로봇 공학과 인공지능(AI) 같은 첨단 기술이 융합되고 있음을 의미하므로 정답은 ⑤가 가장 알맞다. ① 과거의 단순한 디자인으로 돌아가고 있다는 내용은 본문의 흐름과 반대이다. ② 인간의 통제 없이 완벽하게 작동하고 있다는 것은 생각으로 통제하고 있다는 내용이므로 알맞지 않다. ③ 기능보다 외형에 더 집중하고 있다는 것은 언급되지 않았다. ④ 인간 신체의 완전한 유기적 일부가 되고 있다는 내용은 논지와 어긋난다.

The success of AI-powered neural implants in health care is also expected to spread to other industries. Some futurists predict that these implants will become commercially available in the next 20 to 30 years and significantly change our daily lives. For example, advances in neural implant technology will make it possible to install in our brains software that can read our minds. This could enable us to play games, type social media messages, and stream music simply by thinking. There is also great potential for memory-enhancing brain implants, similar to computer memory chips. Such devices would allow us to capture and enhance memories, and even upload and download them using the digital cloud. We could look through our memories like a social media feed, vividly recall our favorite life moments, share memories with others, and back up our most valuable memories. Finally, AI- powered neural implants would revolutionize the way our brains work. The role of the brain would shift from learning and storing information to processing the vast amounts of data provided by the implants. Instead of simply memorizing information, we would be able to download knowledge, use our creativity to interpret it, and generate new ideas.

Before we can fully embrace the era of AI- powered neural implants, many tricky ethical issues should be addressed. However, an over-reliance on technology may delay our natural development and create confusion about whether we are human, AI, or something in between. Another critical issue is privacy. There's a risk that organizations or hackers could access personal data without permission through AI- connected implants. This means that our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors could be controlled by hackers. 이 기술이 모든 사람에게 이용 가능하지 않을 수도 있다는 점을 고려할 때, 이 기술이 훨씬 더 큰 사회적 불평등으로 이어질 수 있다는 추가적인 위험 이 있다. Such unequal access to the technology could intensify the division between those who can afford the implants and those who cannot.
조건 1. 접속사(given that)를 사용할 것
2. (There's, an additional risk, this technology, could lead to, even greater social inequality, available to all, its high cost)를 모두 포함할 것
3. 주어진 단어를 모두 활용할 것

solution: ~라는 점을 고려할 때'라는 의미의 접속사 'given that'을 활용하여 부사절을 구성한다. 조건 1에서 'given that'은 박스에서 제외되었으므로 학생이 직접 써야 한다. 박스에 제공된 'There's an additional risk'로 주절을 시작하고, 'this technology could lead to even greater social inequality'로 위험의 내용을 이어 쓴다. 그 뒤 'given that it may not be available to all due to its high cost'를 붙여 이유를 나타내는 부사절을 완성한다. 박스의 모든 단어가 정답 문장에 그대로 포함되어야 한다.
